description: Hi everyone! 🚀 I’m interested in AI/ML, Web Development & Earth Science. For NASA’s “Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots” challenge, I plan to build an AI-powered wildfire monitoring platform featuring satellite data harmonization, interactive fire maps, historical activity calendars, and anomaly detection. I’m looking for teammates skilled in AI/ML, Python, Web Development, UI/UX, Data Analysis & Visualization. Let’s collaborate and build something innovative! 🌍🔥
summary:
FireFusion AI: Harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS Hotspots
FireFusion AI is an interactive web-based fire intelligence platform that harmonizes NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite active-fire observations into a unified and explorable fire map.
MODIS and VIIRS detect fires at different spatial resolutions and observation times, which can lead to inconsistent hotspot records. Our platform addresses this challenge through transparent spatial and temporal matching, helping users identify confirmed matches, ambiguous observations, and unmatched detections without forcing uncertain results.
Users can explore interactive fire maps, compare satellite observations, examine historical fire activity, and understand detection patterns through data-grounded explanations.
Using NASA FIRMS open data, FireFusion AI aims to make satellite fire observations more accessible, interpretable, and useful for researchers, environmental scientists, educators, and disaster-management stakeholders.
Our goal is to transform complex satellite observations into clearer, more transparent, and actionable fire intelligence while communicating uncertainty and scientific limitations.
details:
FireFusion AI

FireFusion AI is an interactive satellite-based fire intelligence platform developed to address the challenge of harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS active-fire hotspot observations.

How It Works

The platform integrates NASA FIRMS active-fire datasets from MODIS (Terra and Aqua) and VIIRS. Since these satellites have different spatial resolutions and observation times, their detections may overlap or differ.

FireFusion AI applies a transparent spatial and temporal matching methodology to identify:

  • Confirmed one-to-one matched observations.
  • Ambiguous observations with multiple possible matches.
  • Unmatched detections from individual sensors.
  • Duplicate source records where applicable.

The platform presents this information through an interactive fire map, historical activity views, satellite comparison tools, and data-grounded explanations.

Benefits and Intended Impact

FireFusion AI helps researchers, environmental scientists, students, and disaster-management stakeholders understand satellite fire observations more clearly. It reduces confusion caused by inconsistent satellite detection counts and makes fire activity easier to explore and interpret.

The project emphasizes transparency, reproducibility, and uncertainty rather than making unsupported claims about the exact number of real-world fires or predicting future wildfires.

Technologies and Tools

  • Python for data processing and harmonization.
  • Pandas and NumPy for data analysis.
  • Scikit-learn BallTree for spatial matching.
  • GeoPandas and Shapely for geographical processing.
  • React and Vite for the web application.
  • Interactive mapping and data visualization technologies.
  • NASA FIRMS for satellite active-fire data.
  • Vercel for public deployment.

Creativity and Innovation

The innovative aspect of FireFusion AI is its transparent approach to combining observations from two different satellite systems. Instead of simply displaying separate hotspot maps, it explains where observations agree, where they differ, and where matching remains uncertain.

Its goal is to transform complex satellite observations into an accessible and scientifically interpretable fire intelligence experience.
